full_text:
Thank you for working on this, Adam!

A few comments - at least some of which are issues you inherited from the original version.

**##Requirements**

The numbering is a bit odd - I'd probably try to arrange it so that the 6 keys are each numbered, and the other comments are not numbered at all?

1) I'd note that you can use subkey to generate them (as now) but also that you could use the polkadot.js wallet (or another wallet I guess) to generate the stash and controller addresses, and the rotateKeys node method to generate and manage the session keys. [We should probably strongly recommend the rotateKeys option...]

6) Existential balance - I think this has always been wrong.  I'm pretty sure the existential balance in 10 µEDG, with is 0.00001 or 10,000,000,000,000.

7) Ideally the node should be synced before declaring intent to validate in the ##Validate section.

**##Pre-requisites**

Maybe add an "if you plan to use it" next to subkey, and some link or other info for the polkadot.js wallet?

**##Onboarding**
Maybe at the end reiterate that you can also generate the session keys with the rotateKeys method.

**##Validating**
Reference to "v099 testnet" should be "Edgeware".

Amend:  "To insert existing session keys, _if you generated them manually with subkey_, you can run for each key the following command while your node is running:"

This paragraph: "After running these `curl` commands, you should receive as output from `stdout` the public keys you provided \(or didn't\) in a JSON string. That also means the process was a success! You should now see yourself in the list of newly/pending validators to go into effect in future sessions. In the next era \(up to 1 hour\), if there is a slot available, your node will become an active validator."

I'm not sure the second curl command outputs the keys back in JSON - I've never used it.  Have you tried it?  That's certainly what the first command does.

And the node doesn't appear in the pending validator list until the "setup validator" transactions happens, I think.

##Submitting the setKeys Transaction
I think this is actually the dialog you get with "Change session keys" on the Network-->Staking-->Accounts page - which you can't do until you've declared the intend to validate.  Should probably be moved to the end and noted that this is how to change the session keys (along with generating new keys with rotateKeys).

Also add the note that changing the keys on an elected validator takes two sessions (2 hours) to happen.

##Setup via validator

The "allow new nominations" option isn't available on Edgeware, unfortunately.  This probably needs an image change (perhaps just cut the "allow new nominations box out of the picture...).

Last paragraph but one - DOT should be EDG.

The only thing I didn't change and am confused about is the paragraph. 

After running these curl commands, you should receive as output from stdout the public keys you provided (or didn't) in a JSON string. That also means the process was a success! You should now see yourself in the list of newly/pending validators to go into effect in future sessions. In the next era (up to 1 hour), if there is a slot available, your node will become an active validator. 

I didn't use the second curl command at all I am pretty sure I did the rotateKeys method, and this is in the original documentation I didn't touch it. What do you suggest we do?
